transcript: If the skin on your arms hangs loose and doesn't feel firm no matter how much you exercise, the problem isn't in the muscle, it's in the thyroid and in inflammation. When the thyroid is sluggish, your metabolism slows down, the skin loses elasticity, and collagen stops being produced at the rate your body needs. Chronic inflammation accelerates the whole process. The skin sags, the arms hang loose, and no exercise can tighten what inflammation keeps destroying from the inside. In our monastery, we use a remedy every morning that helps balance the thyroid and reduce inflammation, boil a glass of water and add half a teaspoon of turmeric, a pinch of black pepper, a piece of fresh ginger and the juice of half a lemon. Drink it warm on an empty stomach. It calms the inflammation that destroys collagen. Pepper multiplies its absorption. Ginger activates circulation and brings nutrients to the skin. And lemon activates the liver, which is where thyroid hormones are processed. Over time, the thyroid balances out, inflammation goes down, and the skin starts to regain firmness. But I want you to understand something. Your thyroid doesn't go out of balance just because of genetics or age. In Chinese medicine, the thyroid is connected to emotions that are not expressed. Every time you silence what you feel, every time you swallow what you wanted to say, the energy of the throat gets blocked, and the thyroid lives exactly there. Chronic stress also alters thyroid hormones directly. That is why there are women who take thyroid medication and their skin is still saggy, because they regulate the hormone. But don't calm what is disregulating it. Write firm skin in the comments.
